en: The auspicious dawn of Śrī Yādavagiri Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha,
composed by Narasiṃhācārya of Śrī Vaṅgīpura:
O Rāma, son of Kausalyā, the morning twilight is now beginning.
Arise, O tiger among men! The daily rites ordained by destiny must be performed. || 1 ||
Arise, arise, Govinda! Arise, O you whose banner is Garuḍa!
Arise, O beloved of Kamalā; bring auspiciousness to the three worlds! 2.
O Mother, who are the wish-fulfilling creeper for the auspicious temple of the Lord of the Mountain;
O Consort of Padma, who are worshipped by Brahmā and the other gods;
O Destroyer of the afflictions of devotees, whose divine form is composed of compassion!
O beloved of Lakṣmī and Nṛsiṃha, may you have a beautiful dawn. 3.
O Jvālā-Nṛsiṃha, embodiment of compassion, divine form,
delighter in yoga, O Nṛsiṃha, ocean of mercy!
O Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha, Pārijāta tree for those who have come for refuge!
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 4.
Those who know the higher and the lower speak of these as the abodes of the Supreme Being: Śrīraṅga, Veṅkaṭamahīdhara, Hastiśaila, and the foremost among them, Śrī Yādavādri.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May you have a most auspicious dawn. 5.
Brahmā and the other foremost of gods, as well as the best of sages,
wait at the gate with various auspicious objects in their hands to serve you, O Narasiṃha, the boat for crossing the ocean of worldly existence.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Nṛhari! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 6.
O ocean of compassion, those who relish the nectar of devotion— such as Prahlāda, Nārada, Parāśara, Puṇḍarīka, Vyāsa, and others— desire service unto you with single-minded hearts.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 7.
Those who take delight in the enjoyment of service unto you— the noble ones headed by Śaṭhajit and others, with Rāmānuja and other venerable gurus as their leaders—
stand here in the courtyard of your house for the sake of service.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 8.
Your devotees, whose minds are attached to your lotus feet,
having performed their morning rites before your cave-dwelling,
resort to it closely out of an intense longing for the sight of you.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 9.
O Narasiṃha, among the ten divine incarnations, the majesty of that divine incarnation is indeed not accessible even to the gods;
it is accessible only through the devotion of the young Dānava Prahlāda.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 10.
O Śrī, you are well-established upon the peak of Yādavādri, as well as on Ahobila and Siṃhācala, the king of auspicious and blessed mountains,
and upon the summits of Vedācala and other such peaks.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 11.

All those who seek desired objects bow with heads bowed in devotion to you, the granter of boons and the fulfiller of desires; and all those seeking service bow with heads bowed in devotion to you, whose two feet are worthy of being served by the virtuous.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 12.
By the recitation of the mantra of your name, sins roll away; by the recitation of the mantra of your name, demons roll away;
by the recitation of the mantra of your name, diseases roll away.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Nṛhari! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 13.
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha! Lord of the world! Lord of the gods! Viṣṇu, Jiṣṇu, Janārdana! O Supreme beyond the supreme, whose form is the universe!
You who have taken incarnation for the purpose of bringing forth the awakening of the world.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Nṛhari! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 14.
By the recitation of the mantra of your name, may there indeed be a beautiful dawn for us, and may there be a beautiful dawn for you as well;
may there be the very deliverance from our wondrous and profound [suffering].
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail. 15.
Your worshippers and attendants, who have been fully immersed [in devotion] and who perform their own duties according to the rules for the sake of constant worship,
stand before your auspicious cave-temple.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Nṛhari! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 16.
Preparing their morning offerings and bringing forward full water-pitchers,
the Śrīvaiṣṇavas approach, O Hari, O Nṛsiṃha!
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 17.
The sun rises, the day-lotuses bloom,
and indeed the blue lotuses close;
the multitude of the sun's rays emerges from the eastern quarter.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May you have a most auspicious dawn. 18.
The gentle breeze, having slowly entered the interiors of the lotuses in the celestial river and imparting a beautiful fragrance,
attains the height of joy to serve you.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Nṛhari! May your auspicious dawn prevail. 19.
The host of stars in the sky dissolves at this beautiful dawn as they gaze together with the sun upon your glorious,
auspicious morning that illuminates all the world.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Nṛhari! May your auspicious dawn be upon me. 20.
Birds are flying all around, and flocks of cuckoos are warbling with their sweet-voiced calls;
the kīras repeat [the words] with pure-toned speech.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Nṛhari! May your auspicious dawn prevail. 21.
In the hamlets, the cowherds milk their cows in the courtyards of their own homes, beholding them with a special vision,
just as one gazes upon a cowherd boy within the lotuses of the hearts of devotees.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May there be a beautiful dawn for you. 22.
The dense mass of darkness leaves the sky,
just as the darkness of delusion leaves a virtuous man;
passion completely withdraws, just as dispassion does.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 23.
For sleep leaves ordinary people just as wisdom arises in them, while it leaves the sage just as it does not arise in him;
for attachment remains with ordinary people, while detachment remains with the sage.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 24.
O Pure Being, just as groves of lotuses bloom, so too do the lotus-hearts of the virtuous blossom;
like the sun, O Pure Being, you shine resplendent in every direction and intermediate quarter.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Nṛhari! May your auspicious dawn prevail. 25.
Brahmā, together with the hosts of gods and the guardians of the worlds, having entered your abode adorned with pavilions and gate-towers,
extols the fivefold purity of yours.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Nṛhari! May your auspicious dawn prevail. 26.
Afflicted by disease, people— deceived by the web of illnesses and by those who are renowned as famous physicians— determine you to be a famous physician and come from afar to your abode.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 27.
O Lord, those afflicted by the intense torment of elemental spirits, planetary grahas, and the like, and pierced by the most fierce piśācas headed by Bāṇāvatī,
come to you for refuge after bathing and performing circumambulations.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail. 28.
O God of gods, bestower of excellent progeny, women devoid of offspring, having bathed in your lake with their garments wet from the water, come to behold you.
O Nṛhari, Lord of Yādādri, may you have a most auspicious dawn! 29.
O Great Narasiṃha, that form of Yours which destroys the wicked, protects the highest worlds, and manifests initiation—
that very same form shines here upon the head of the mountain.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 30.
O Prahlāda, O source of merit, by the power of your merit, people perceive Your form which is known through the Upanishads;
remembering it at dawn, one crosses the ocean of worldly existence.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail! 31.
May this auspicious *Suprabhātam*, spoken by Acyuta under a pretext, remain infallible (*acyuta*)— it is to be known solely by His devotees—
through the power of the auspicious name of Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha.
O Lord of the Mountain, O Man-Lion! May your auspicious dawn prevail. || 32 ||
Thus, those men who, free from sloth, always recite this "Fair Dawn" of the Lord of Mountains with devotion shall be partakers of happiness. (33)
Thus ends the glorious *Lakṣmī-narasiṃha-suprabhātam*.
